forces.title: Improved air access supports Irish tourism and inbound recovery.
forces.description: Improved air access has significantly supported inbound recovery for Ireland, with trips to the country increasing by 18% year-on-year in the five months to May 2026. European trips were up 24%, and North American trips rose by 15%. This surge in holiday and business travel acts as a strong tailwind for Irish airports, driving higher passenger volumes and associated aeronautical and non-aeronautical revenues, crucial for sustained growth and profitability in the sector.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Dublin Airport cap removal boosts air traffic and capacity.
forces.description: The removal of Dublin Airport's passenger cap led to a 15% increase in air seat capacity over winter, with a projected 3% increase for summer 2026 (including 9% from the US). This policy change is a significant tailwind for the airport, allowing for higher throughput, increased aeronautical revenues, and greater non-aeronautical spending, supporting overall operational growth and economic contribution. It enables the airport to better meet surging demand and capitalize on tourism recovery.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Post-pandemic passenger surge strains airport capacity globally.
forces.description: Airports globally are experiencing passenger volumes exceeding pre-pandemic levels. However, capacity remains severely strained due to persistent labor shortages, new sustainability mandates, and significant delays in planned infrastructure projects. This creates operational bottlenecks and limits airports' ability to efficiently handle the increased demand, putting pressure on service quality and the potential for further growth within existing footprints, representing a major operational headwind.
forces.source_title: The AI Nervous System Guiding Leading Airports

forces.title: Global air travel demand continues robust, supports airport growth.
forces.description: Airports are critical infrastructure, and global demand for air travel remains strong and growing. This consistent demand provides a fundamental tailwind for airport operators, ensuring a steady stream of passenger traffic. It underpins revenue generation from both aeronautical charges and non-aeronautical retail/concessions, supporting long-term investment viability and operational stability despite evolving challenges in capacity and operational efficiency, showcasing the inherent attractiveness of the sector.
forces.source_title: The AI Nervous System Guiding Leading Airports

forces.title: Fragmented planning hinders airport operational efficiency across stakeholders.
forces.description: Airport operations are characterized by fragmented planning across numerous stakeholders, including airport owners, airlines, ground handlers, and air traffic control. Each entity often prioritizes its own objectives, leading to inefficiencies, bottlenecks, and suboptimal system-wide performance. This lack of integrated decision-making and conflicting incentives creates a fundamental structural challenge that airports must address to achieve seamless operations and maximize throughput, requiring a unified approach to overcome ingrained silos.
forces.source_title: The AI Nervous System Guiding Leading Airports

forces.title: Aging infrastructure elevates maintenance costs, degrades airport service.
forces.description: Many airports are grappling with aging infrastructure, which directly leads to higher maintenance costs and a gradual degradation of service quality. This issue acts as a significant headwind, requiring substantial capital expenditure for repairs and upgrades to maintain operational standards and passenger satisfaction. It also diverts resources that could otherwise be invested in capacity expansion or new technologies, creating a drag on profitability and operational modernization efforts over the long term.
forces.source_title: The AI Nervous System Guiding Leading Airports

forces.title: Frequent disruptions reduce airport operational resilience and buffers.
forces.description: Airports are experiencing an increased frequency of disruptions, ranging from extreme weather to geopolitical events, which leaves them with reduced operational buffers. This heightened volatility poses a key risk, making it more challenging to maintain punctuality, manage passenger flows, and recover quickly from irregular events. It stresses existing infrastructure and personnel, potentially leading to cascading delays and increased costs, demanding greater adaptability and robust contingency planning from airport operators.
forces.source_title: The AI Nervous System Guiding Leading Airports

forces.title: Disconnected AI initiatives hinder airport transformation and value.
forces.description: Airports often implement AI initiatives in a fragmented manner, focusing on numerous small use cases rather than strategic, end-to-end operational flows. This disconnected approach limits their ability to achieve transformative improvements, leading to only incremental gains and failing to address core business challenges effectively. It represents a headwind in realizing the full potential of digital investment due to a lack of integrated strategy and systemic impact, necessitating a more cohesive deployment plan.
forces.source_title: The AI Nervous System Guiding Leading Airports

forces.title: Data silos obstruct unified airport operations and transparency.
forces.description: A significant structural challenge for airports is the persistence of data silos among individual stakeholders, where separate systems are maintained, and data sharing is limited. This fragmentation prevents the creation of a real-time, shared operational view across the entire airport ecosystem, hindering coordinated decision-making and effective response to disruptions. It limits overall transparency and efficiency, making it difficult to implement system-wide improvements and realize the benefits of digital integration.
forces.source_title: The AI Nervous System Guiding Leading Airports

forces.title: Insufficient data infrastructure hampers airport AI solution scalability.
forces.description: Despite promising pilot projects for AI and digital solutions, airports face a critical headwind: limited reliable data infrastructure. This inadequacy prevents the widespread scaling of successful initiatives across the entire airport ecosystem, as the foundational data models and integration capabilities are often insufficient. It restricts the realization of broader operational improvements and value creation from technological investments, demanding strategic investment in robust data foundations to unlock full potential.
forces.source_title: The AI Nervous System Guiding Leading Airports

forces.title: Digital nervous systems enhance airport orchestration and performance.
forces.description: The implementation of a digital nervous system, incorporating a shared data layer and a "single plan" operating model, acts as a significant upside driver for airports. This system enables end-to-end orchestration across all operational facets—ground, airside, passenger, baggage, and commercial ventures—leading to real-time decision-making. It improves operational performance and commercial outcomes by unifying information and streamlining processes, making airports more efficient, resilient, and better equipped to handle increasing demand.
forces.source_title: The AI Nervous System Guiding Leading Airports

forces.title: Stricter sustainability policies moderate European airport traffic growth.
forces.description: European airports face a headwind from potentially stricter sustainability policies, including mandates for sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and expanded emissions trading schemes. These regulations, while necessary for environmental goals, are expected to moderate overall traffic growth. This could increase operational costs for airlines and indirectly for airports, influencing route decisions and passenger demand, contributing to a more challenging growth environment and requiring airports to adapt their long-term development strategies.
forces.source_title: European Airports Add New Routes to Value Creation

forces.title: LCC expansion reshapes European airport traffic and revenue.
forces.description: The continued expansion of low-cost carriers (LCCs) in Europe, replacing full-service carrier capacity and growing in Tier 3 airports, constitutes a structural change. LCCs seek lower charges and flexible infrastructure, impacting airport revenue structures. While they drive volume, they also increase competitive pressure and volatility, as LCCs can quickly alter routes and constantly push for more favorable terms, challenging traditional aeronautical revenue models and forcing airports to adapt pricing strategies.
forces.source_title: European Airports Add New Routes to Value Creation

forces.title: Over-reliance on LCCs introduces revenue volatility for airports.
forces.description: Small and midsize European airports increasingly rely on low-cost carriers (LCCs) for traffic volume. However, this dependence poses a key risk due to LCCs' tendency to quickly change routes and aggressively negotiate for lower airport charges. This creates revenue volatility and puts continuous pressure on aeronautical income, making it challenging for airports to achieve stable and sustainable financial performance and necessitating diversification strategies to mitigate this risk.
forces.source_title: European Airports Add New Routes to Value Creation

forces.title: Non-European FSCs expand long-haul, diversifying non-hub airport traffic.
forces.description: The expansion of non-European full-service carriers (FSCs) into long-haul markets, driven by new trade lanes and faster capacity expansion, presents an upside driver for European airports. Coupled with the introduction of long-haul narrowbody aircraft, this trend creates new opportunities for larger non-hub airports to diversify their traffic beyond intra-European flights, potentially attracting higher-yield passengers and new revenue streams, reducing reliance on short-haul LCC traffic and enhancing overall market position.
forces.source_title: European Airports Add New Routes to Value Creation

forces.title: Outdated non-aeronautical models pressure airport commercial revenue.
forces.description: Non-aeronautical revenues, derived from parking, retail, dining, and advertising, face pressure from outdated commercial models and offerings that no longer align with evolving passenger demand. This acts as a headwind, limiting the potential for growth and profitability in a key revenue segment for airports. Modernization of commercial strategies and retail mix is crucial to capture passenger spending effectively, as passengers seek more relevant and convenient services, impacting revenue per passenger metrics.
forces.source_title: European Airports Add New Routes to Value Creation

forces.title: Rising OpEx pressures airport margins from labor and energy.
forces.description: Over 50% of surveyed European airports are persistently concerned by rising operating expenses (OpEx), which are increasing at approximately 1% above inflation. This headwind is primarily driven by elevated labor costs due to specialist shortages, as well as higher energy and material expenses. This cost inflation erodes airport profitability, necessitating efficiency improvements and strategic cost management to maintain financial health and competitiveness in a challenging economic environment.
forces.source_title: European Airports Add New Routes to Value Creation

forces.title: Large European airports operate at or near full declared capacity.
forces.description: Many large European airports, especially those handling over 20 million passengers annually, are operating at 90% to 100% of their declared capacity. This structural condition means limited room for growth within existing infrastructure, leading to bottlenecks and potential service degradation during peak times. It underscores the urgent need for either capacity expansion or significant efficiency improvements through technology to manage growing demand and avoid operational constraints that could hinder future traffic growth.
forces.source_title: European Airports Add New Routes to Value Creation

forces.title: Neighboring hubs expand aggressively, intensify intercontinental competition.
forces.description: European airports face a significant headwind from major hubs in neighboring regions like Istanbul, Doha, Dubai, and Riyadh. These airports are aggressively expanding their capacity and services, directly aiming to capture a larger share of intercontinental traffic. This increased competition puts pressure on EU hubs to remain competitive in long-haul and connecting markets, potentially diverting traffic and revenue away from European operators and challenging their strategic positioning in global aviation networks.
forces.source_title: European Airports Add New Routes to Value Creation

forces.title: Investor caution on airports creates financing hurdles.
forces.description: Investors have become more cautious towards airports, posing a significant headwind to financing essential infrastructure and improvement projects. This shift reflects a decline in airport Total Shareholder Returns (TSRs) by 13 percentage points since the pandemic, as other asset classes like renewables and telecoms have become more attractive. This caution adds a hurdle for airports seeking capital for modernization and capacity expansion, impacting long-term growth and the ability to compete effectively in a capital-intensive industry.
forces.source_title: European Airports Add New Routes to Value Creation

forces.title: Stabilizing investor sentiment aids airport infrastructure financing.
forces.description: Investor sentiment towards airports has shown a gradual improvement from post-pandemic lows, now stabilizing in line with other infrastructure asset classes. This tailwind suggests a return of confidence in the sector, making it easier for airports to attract financing for critical infrastructure projects and improvements. This renewed stability is essential for long-term capital-intensive developments, easing previous financing hurdles and supporting the necessary investments for modernization and capacity expansion across European airports.
forces.source_title: European Airports Add New Routes to Value Creation

forces.title: Digital and AI adoption drives efficiency and EBITDA gains for airports.
forces.description: Over 90% of large European airports prioritize digital transformation and AI-enabled tools to enhance efficiency, expand capacity within existing infrastructure, and mitigate OpEx pressures. This widespread adoption is a strong upside driver, with transformation programs already delivering material results, including up to 3 percentage points of EBITDA improvement. These technologies, like optimized gate allocation and predictive maintenance, unlock latent capacity and improve service quality, positioning airports for more resilient and profitable operations.
forces.source_title: European Airports Add New Routes to Value Creation

forces.title: Airports optimize traffic mix for resilience and higher yields.
forces.description: Nearly 90% of midsize European airports are actively rebalancing their traffic mix, shifting away from over-reliance on specific carriers towards higher-yield segments like long-haul and premium leisure travel. This structural change is driven by the realization that volume alone is insufficient for sustained margins. It enhances resilience and aims to increase revenue per passenger, adapting to market pressures and fostering more profitable growth, fundamentally altering how airports manage their airline relationships and route development.
forces.source_title: European Airports Add New Routes to Value Creation

forces.title: Airports rethink commercial strategies to boost non-aeronautical revenue.
forces.description: Almost half of European airports are actively rethinking their commercial strategies to boost non-aeronautical revenues per passenger. This represents a significant upside driver, with initiatives projected to increase non-aero revenues by 5% to 10% over the next decade. Strategies include strengthening F&B, revamping retail footprints with flexible formats, introducing omnichannel retail, personalized offers, and flexible concession models tied to performance, vital for stabilizing performance amidst declining aero revenues and enhancing overall profitability.
forces.source_title: European Airports Add New Routes to Value Creation

forces.title: Ecosystem collaboration crucial for enhanced airport value creation.
forces.description: To unlock and amplify value, European airports require collaboration among all stakeholders: airlines, commercial partners, investors, regulators, and public institutions. This upside driver involves improved data sharing, closer operational coordination, and aligned commercial and regulatory frameworks. Such collaborative efforts are essential to enhance operational efficiency, strengthen commercial performance, and address structural misalignments, leading to system-wide benefits and sustained long-term value for all players within the aviation ecosystem, positioning airports as central orchestrators.
forces.source_title: European Airports Add New Routes to Value Creation

viewpoints.title: Dublin Airport capacity surge improves Irish tourism and economy.
viewpoints.description: Bank of Ireland notes a 15% increase in air seat capacity into Ireland this winter following Dublin Airport's passenger cap removal. Summer 2026 access is projected to be 3% above Summer 2025 levels, including 9% growth from the US. This increased air access is a positive development for Dublin Airport operators, driving higher passenger volumes and benefiting the wider Irish economy by supporting inbound tourism expenditure. This indicates a favorable operational environment for the airport and associated tourism businesses.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

viewpoints.title: European airports face challenging operating environment despite strong traffic rebound.
viewpoints.description: While European airports have seen a strong rebound in passenger traffic post-pandemic, the operating environment is becoming increasingly challenging. Structural changes are pressuring sector economics, impacting the long-term outlook, and hindering investment crucial for sustaining infrastructure and service levels. This collective dynamic could put between €45 billion and €75 billion of cumulative EBITDA at risk across the European airport industry over the next two decades, equivalent to a potential margin decline of up to 10 percentage points.
viewpoints.source_title: European Airports Add New Routes to Value Creation

pnl_drivers.description: Optimized operations through digital nervous systems allow for better capacity utilization, reducing delays and increasing aircraft movements, directly boosting aeronautical tariffs and charges.

Improved passenger flow management and predictive intelligence lead to increased dwell time in retail areas and personalized offers, maximizing spend per passenger on retail, dining, and other concessions.
Real-time decision-making, predictive maintenance, and optimized resource allocation achieved through digital systems lead to significant cost savings in labor, energy, and materials.

new_opportunities.description: By maximizing throughput and efficiency within existing infrastructure using AI and digital tools, airports can postpone or entirely avoid the need for costly new infrastructure projects, optimizing capital allocation.

market_sizing.methodology: Analysis of digital nervous system optimizations impacting core airport value pools, including increased aeronautical revenue, increased non-aeronautical revenue, reduced operating expenses, and deferred or avoided capital expenses. These improvements arise from better capacity utilization, improved passenger flow, predictive maintenance, and optimized resource allocation.
market_sizing.source_title: The AI Nervous System Guiding Leading Airports

new_opportunities.description: Using AI/ML models to assign flights, especially high-value passengers, to gates near retail areas, can increase gate utilization, reduce disruptions, improve ground crew schedules, and significantly boost commercial revenue for airports.

market_sizing.methodology: Estimated annual value potential for a leading Nordic airport through optimized gate and stand allocation using AI and machine learning models in a 10-week proof of concept. Benefits also include fewer flight disruptions, better ground crew schedules, and higher retail sales.
market_sizing.source_title: The AI Nervous System Guiding Leading Airports

pnl_drivers.description: Changes in airline strategies and passenger preferences, including increased reliance on LCCs and expansion into Tier 3 airports, impact the mix and profitability of airport traffic.
Declining real aeronautical charges due to LCC growth and tariff frameworks, coupled with outdated non-aeronautical commercial models, reduce revenue per passenger.
Increases in labor costs (due to shortages) and energy/materials expenses drive operating expenditure growth above inflation, eroding margins.
The need for significant capital expenditure to upgrade, modernize, and expand aging and constrained infrastructure at increasing costs puts pressure on financial performance.

market_sizing.methodology: Cumulative EBITDA at risk across the European airport industry over the next two decades (2026-2046) due to four structural pressures: shifting traffic patterns, unit revenue pressures, rising operating costs, and high investment requirements.
market_sizing.source_title: European Airports Add New Routes to Value Creation

pnl_drivers.description: Post-pandemic labor shortages, particularly of specialists, are projected to drive labor costs up, impacting operational profitability.

market_sizing.methodology: Real labor costs per passenger (personnel and contracted services) for European airports. Declined from €16 in 2015 to €13 in 2023. Forecasted to rise by 0.6% annually in real terms.
market_sizing.source_title: European Airports Add New Routes to Value Creation

demand_drivers.description: Strong underlying demand for air travel continues to drive passenger volumes, with a projected increase of 940 million passengers by 2030 compared to 2015.

market_sizing.methodology: Projected increase in European airport passenger traffic by 2030 compared to 2015 levels. Highlights a significant gap between demand and expected capacity growth.
market_sizing.source_title: European Airports Add New Routes to Value Creation
